news.title: Declan Rice accepts he had an ‘average World Cup’ as England gear up for Spain showdown
news.lede: Midfielder needed a break ‘to come back stronger’. James Trafford selected to start in goal for England. Declan Rice has admitted he had an “average” World Cup at the end of a gruelling season and needed time out during the international window in September and October in order to return stronger. The Arsenal midfielder believes the break has served its purpose, having produced starring performances against Bayern Munich and Liverpool in recent weeks.

news.title: Spain v England: Nations League test will reveal if Thomas Tuchel has learned lessons
news.lede: England head coach Thomas Tuchel during the World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina in Atlanta. England's proof of progress and the lessons learned by head coach Thomas Tuchel since the disappointment of World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina will be put to the sternest test when they face holders Spain in Madrid. Spain present the toughest assignment England could face, with the world champions' unbeaten run – in which they claimed the sport's biggest prize by beating Argentina in New Jersey in the summer – now stretching to 43 games. Luis de la Fuente's side last lost - to Colombia - in March 2024, winning 34 games and drawing nine in the intervening period, during which they also became European champions, beating England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.

news.title: 2030 World Cup final will be held in Spain – RFEF president insists
news.lede: Spain will host the final of the 2030 FIFA World Cup, Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) president Rafael Louzán has reiterated. Spain is co-hosting the tournament with Portugal and Morocco, but FIFA is expected to decide on the venue for the final by 2028. Read Also: FIFA considers expanding 2030 World Cup to 66 teams. “There is no other plan than for the final to be held in Spain,” Louzán said on Saturday at a conference held at the RFEF’s Ciudad del Fútbol headquarters on the outskirts of Madrid.

news.title: Before the 2030 World Cup: Spain face a new test off the pitch
news.lede: Competition to host the final stage of the UEFA Nations League continues, but this time away from the pitch, after Spain and France entered a fierce race to organise the "Final Four" tournament scheduled to take place next June. The deadline for submitting bid files closed on 21 October, and Spain and France appear to be the frontrunners to host the tournament, according to the newspaper "Marca". The Spanish Football Federation submitted a strong bid featuring two stadiums, the Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid and the José Zorrilla in Valladolid, while the French Federation is competing with the stadiums in Lyon and Saint-Étienne to host the matches. Nothing will be settled before the quarter-final draw on 20 November.

news.title: Spanish football federation president says hosting 2030 World Cup final in Spain is ‘non-negotiable’
news.lede: Spanish Football Federation President Rafael Louzán on Saturday renewed Spain’s push to host the 2030 World Cup final, saying that holding the match in Spain was “not negotiable.” Speaking on the sidelines of a conference in Madrid, Louzán said the decision on the final’s venue would be made in 2028. But he emphasized that the Spanish federation could not see the match being played outside Spain and had “no other roadmap” on the matter. Louzán said the World Cup “belongs to Europe, Spain and Portugal,” without mentioning Morocco, which is co-hosting the tournament and is also seeking to host the final.

news.title: "Pack your bags and get out!" World Cup-winning legend tears into Carlo Ancelotti after defeat
news.lede: Brazil national team coach Carlo Ancelotti is under pressure after a 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan, with World Cup winner Romario calling on Instagram for the Italian to be sacked immediately.The former world-class striker's criticism followed a friendly in Singapore that brought a late defeat for the Selecao and acts of indiscipline.Against Japan, the record World Cup winners were already two goals behind after less than 20 minutes. Vinicius Junior scored twice to bring his side level, but Tatsuhiro Sakamoto struck the winner for Japan in stoppage time.Brazil's bench protested fiercely over the build-up to the late goal, believing they had spotted an earlier foul. The referee allowed the goal to stand, then showed both national team coach Ancelotti and the already-substituted attacking player Raphinha red cards for their behaviour.Romario, 60, vented his anger on Instagram.
